parameters.name: ClientToken
parameters.description: A client token that ensures the idempotence of a request. Generate a unique value for this parameter on your client. The value can be up to 64 ASCII characters in length.

parameters.name: Priority
parameters.description: The priority of the MX record. A smaller value indicates a higher priority. The value can be an integer from 1 to 99.

parameters.name: RecordId
parameters.description: The ID of the DNS record.

parameters.name: RequestSource
parameters.description:
The resolution line. The default value is **default**. For more information, see:

[Lines](https://help.aliyun.com/document_detail/29807.html)

</props>

<props="intl">

parameters.name: Rr
parameters.description:
The host record. This is the prefix of a domain name. Common prefixes are www, @, \* for wildcard DNS, and mail for mailboxes.

For example, to resolve @.example.com, set the host record to "@". Do not leave it empty.

parameters.name: Ttl
parameters.description: The Time to Live (TTL) in seconds. Only the following values are supported: 5, 30, 60, 3600 (1 hour), 43200 (12 hours), and 86400 (24 hours). The default value is 60.

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description: The type of the DNS record. The following types are supported: A: An IPv4 record that maps a domain name to an IPv4 address. AAAA: An IPv6 record that maps a domain name to an IPv6 address. CNAME: An alias record that points a domain name to another domain name. MX: A mail exchanger record that points a domain name to a mail server address. TXT: A text record that contains arbitrary human-readable text. SRV: A service record that identifies a server for a specific service. This is common in directory management for Microsoft systems.

parameters.name: Value
parameters.description: The record value. Enter a value that corresponds to the DNS record type.

parameters.name: Weight
parameters.description: The weight. An integer from 1 to 100, inclusive. The default value is 1. You can set different weights for each address. DNS queries return addresses in proportion to their weights.
